description: A wolf the moon keeps. Its silver fur holds the crescent's mark, and its paws never quite touch the frost.
lore: [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] walks between fires after dark, which a man his age has been told not to do, and he has not been alone doing it for eleven winters. Something falls in behind him a little way out and holds thirty paces — exactly thirty, over broken ground and through water — and comes as far as the edge of the light and no farther. Silver, a blue crescent set in the fur of the brow, seams of cold colour down the shoulders. He calls it his escort and means it.

Look at the frost under it. There is a hand's width of nothing there, no print in the rime, and after a night in new snow the road behind Wendell shows one set of boots. He knows what that is. It has let go of the ground the way you let go of a name, and what goes after the ground goes fast.

So he talks to it the whole way. Not chatter — proper tellings: the east road when it was still walked, his sister's stubbornness, the winter the wells went strange. Others say a telling wants somebody listening and an animal is not somebody. Wendell answers that it walks when he talks and stops when he stops, and that this will have to do, and that he could not tell you which of the two of them is holding the other up anyway. Both of them are still here. He considers the argument closed.
gm_notes: Shipped description adopted verbatim from the monsters agent — it is accurate to the art (crescent brow-mark, cyan seams, sparkle under the paws) and better than anything I had. The record's load-bearing question is whether a telling to an animal counts under Law II; leave it unanswered forever. Wendell's escort is a Habit-stage animal that has forgotten weight, so it leaves no evidence and therefore almost nobody tells about it, which is why it is thinning. Do not let a player prove it either way.
